item.content:encoded:
Are you passionate about understanding how social inequality shapes educational opportunities and life outcomes? Do you have a strong academic background in sociology, interdisciplinary social science, or a related field? Utrecht University in the Netherlands is inviting applications for a fully funded PhD position in Contextual (Dis)advantage and Educational Inequality within its renowned Faculty of Social and Behavioural Sciences.

This four-year doctoral opportunity offers aspiring researchers the chance to conduct cutting-edge research on how family, neighbourhood, and school environments interact to influence children’s educational success. Successful applicants will receive a competitive salary, excellent employment benefits, international research opportunities, and professional development while working at one of Europe’s leading research universities.

If you are looking to pursue a PhD in sociology, educational inequality, or social science research in Europe, this is an excellent opportunity to advance your academic career.

About the PhD Project

Educational inequality remains one of the most important social challenges worldwide. While previous research has examined how individual environments such as families, schools, or neighbourhoods affect educational outcomes, this PhD project aims to go one step further.

Rather than studying these environments separately, the research investigates how different social contexts interact and influence one another. The project explores whether advantages in one environment can compensate for disadvantages in another—or whether multiple disadvantages combine to create even greater educational inequality.

The successful PhD researcher will investigate questions such as:

  • How do children become part of different educational and social environments?
  • How do family background, neighbourhoods, and schools jointly influence educational achievement?
  • How do multiple forms of socio-economic and ethnic disadvantage shape life opportunities?
  • Can certain contexts reduce or amplify educational inequalities?

The project combines advanced quantitative social science with innovative research methods to better understand educational inequality using extensive Dutch population register data.

Research Focus Areas

The doctoral project focuses on several important research themes, including:

  • Educational inequality
  • Socio-economic inequality
  • Ethnic inequality
  • Family background
  • School environments
  • Neighbourhood effects
  • Contextual disadvantage
  • Social mobility
  • Educational outcomes
  • Social stratification

The research will make use of:

  • Dutch administrative register data
  • Large-scale datasets
  • Quasi-experimental research designs
  • Quantitative statistical analysis
  • Simulation methods

The findings are expected to contribute significantly to international research on education and social inequality.

Responsibilities of the PhD Candidate

The successful applicant will join the Department of Sociology at Utrecht University and will be expected to contribute actively to research, teaching, and academic life.

Primary responsibilities include:

1. Conduct Original Research

The PhD candidate will:

  • Review existing scientific literature
  • Develop research questions
  • Analyze complex datasets
  • Interpret findings
  • Publish research in international scientific journals
  • Complete a doctoral dissertation

2. Present Research

The researcher will present research findings at:

  • National conferences
  • International conferences
  • Academic workshops
  • Research seminars

3. Participate in Department Activities

The successful candidate will actively engage in:

  • Department seminars
  • Research collaborations
  • Academic meetings
  • Faculty activities

4. Teaching Duties

Teaching responsibilities will account for a maximum of 10% of the appointment and provide valuable university teaching experience.

Who Should Apply?

Utrecht University is seeking motivated and enthusiastic applicants with strong academic potential and a passion for research.

Ideal candidates should have:

  • A completed (or nearly completed) Master’s degree in Sociology, Interdisciplinary Social Science, or a related discipline
  • Strong interest in socio-economic inequality and ethnic inequality
  • Interest in educational research
  • Strong analytical thinking skills
  • Excellent research motivation

The university particularly welcomes applicants interested in quantitative social science research.

Preferred Qualifications

Applicants with the following qualifications will be particularly competitive:

  • Experience with advanced quantitative research methods
  • Experience working with large and complex datasets
  • Strong statistical analysis skills
  • Interest in teaching
  • Ability to publish academic research
  • Excellent scientific writing abilities
  • Good presentation skills
  • Good organizational and interpersonal skills
  • Creativity and initiative
  • Motivation to communicate scientific findings to the wider public

Language requirements include:

  • Excellent written and spoken English
  • Reading proficiency in Dutch is considered an advantage but is not mandatory.

Salary and Employment Benefits

The selected PhD candidate will receive a highly competitive employment package.

Benefits include:

Competitive Salary

Gross monthly salary:

  • First year: €3,204
  • Fourth year: €4,051

The salary increases progressively throughout the four-year appointment.

Employment Contract

The appointment includes:

  • Initial one-year contract
  • Extension to a total of four years following a successful performance assessment
  • Full-time employment (36–40 hours per week)

Additional Benefits

Employees also receive:

  • 8% holiday allowance
  • 8.3% end-of-year bonus
  • Pension scheme
  • Partially paid parental leave
  • Flexible working conditions
  • Professional development opportunities
  • Sports and cultural activities
  • Various leave arrangements
  • Customized employment benefits through Utrecht University’s Terms of Employment Options Model

Why Choose Utrecht University?

Utrecht University is one of Europe’s leading research universities and is internationally recognized for excellence in teaching and scientific research.

Its mission is to create “A better future for everyone” through innovative research and interdisciplinary collaboration.

The university’s strategic research themes include:

  • Dynamics of Youth
  • Institutions for Open Societies
  • Life Sciences
  • Pathways to Sustainability

The Faculty of Social and Behavioural Sciences is among Europe’s leading centres for research and education in:

  • Sociology
  • Psychology
  • Educational Sciences
  • Cultural Anthropology
  • Interdisciplinary Social Science
  • Pedagogical Sciences

The faculty hosts:

  • Nearly 7,000 students
  • Around 1,100 academic and professional staff

The campus is located at Utrecht Science Park, close to the historic city centre of Utrecht in the Netherlands.

Application Documents Required

Applicants must submit the following documents:

  1. Curriculum Vitae (CV)
  2. Letter of Motivation
  3. Overview of Master’s courses completed
  4. Master’s grades/transcript

Applications must be submitted through Utrecht University’s online application system.

International Applicants

International candidates are welcome to apply.

Applicants who require a Dutch visa or work permit should note:

  • Visa processing may take at least four months after selection.
  • Utrecht University’s International Service Desk (ISD) offers guidance on relocating to the Netherlands.
  • Applicants are responsible for arranging their own accommodation, although the ISD may provide advice.

Selection Process

The recruitment process includes:

  • Application review
  • Shortlisting
  • First-round interviews

Interview date:

  • August 21, 2026

Preferred starting date:

  • September or October 2026

Knowledge security screening may form part of the recruitment process.

Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

Utrecht University is committed to building a diverse, inclusive, and welcoming academic community.

The university encourages applications from individuals of all backgrounds, regardless of:

  • Cultural background
  • Religion
  • Ethnicity
  • Gender
  • Sexual orientation
  • Disability
  • Age

Equal opportunity and inclusion are core values throughout the recruitment process.

Click HERE to learn more.

Why You Should Apply

This PhD position provides an outstanding opportunity for aspiring researchers interested in educational inequality, sociology, and quantitative social science.

Successful applicants will benefit from:

  • Four years of funded doctoral research
  • Competitive salary with annual increases
  • International research collaborations
  • Conference participation
  • Academic publishing opportunities
  • University teaching experience
  • Excellent employment benefits
  • Professional development
  • Access to world-class researchers and facilities
  • Opportunity to contribute to policies addressing educational inequality

For candidates seeking a fully funded PhD in Europe focused on educational inequality and social research, this opportunity offers an excellent foundation for a successful academic career.

Application Deadline

Application Deadline: 12 August 2026

Applicants are encouraged to submit their applications well before the deadline to allow sufficient time for preparing all required documents.

APPLY HERE

Conclusion

The PhD in Contextual (Dis)advantage and Educational Inequality at Utrecht University is an exceptional opportunity for talented graduates who wish to pursue advanced research into one of society’s most pressing issues: educational inequality. By combining innovative quantitative research methods with large-scale administrative data, the project aims to generate new insights into how family, school, and neighbourhood contexts shape educational outcomes and life chances.

Beyond conducting impactful research, the successful candidate will receive a competitive salary, comprehensive employment benefits, teaching experience, international networking opportunities, and access to one of Europe’s leading social science faculties. If you have a passion for sociology, inequality research, and evidence-based policy, this fully funded PhD position offers the ideal environment to develop into an accomplished researcher while contributing meaningful knowledge to the field.

item.content:encoded:
Are you passionate about advancing research on gender equality, migration, displacement, and the prevention of violence against women? The Australian National University (ANU) is offering a fully funded PhD Scholarship on Violence Against Women and Displacement for outstanding domestic and international students.

This prestigious opportunity allows scholars to contribute to the Australian Research Council Centre of Excellence for the Elimination of Violence Against Women (CEVAW), one of Australia’s leading research initiatives focused on understanding and preventing violence against women across Australia and the Indo-Pacific region.

The scholarship provides generous financial support, access to world-class researchers, extensive professional development opportunities, and the chance to undertake impactful research that informs policy and practice.

Scholarship Summary

  • Host Country: Australia
  • Host Institution: Australian National University (ANU)
  • Research Centre: Centre of Excellence for the Elimination of Violence Against Women (CEVAW)
  • Study Level: PhD (Higher Degree Research)
  • Eligible Applicants: Domestic and International Students
  • Scholarship Value: AUD $39,069 per annum
  • Application Deadline: August 31, 2026
  • Number of Awards: 1
  • Duration: Standard PhD duration with possible 6-month extension

About the Scholarship

The PhD scholarship is based within the Department of International Relations at the Coral Bell School of Asia Pacific Affairs, ANU.

The successful candidate will conduct research examining violence against women in contexts of migration, displacement, trafficking, conflict, and climate-related disasters. The project will contribute to strengthening the evidence base for preventing and responding to gender-based violence while supporting vulnerable communities across the Indo-Pacific region.

The research stream is led by Professor Bina D’Costa, Chief Investigator at CEVAW, and emphasizes Indigenous-centred and survivor-focused approaches to research.

Applicants are encouraged to develop projects that align with CEVAW’s mission of addressing structural drivers of violence against women and generating practical solutions for communities, governments, and organizations.

Research Areas

Potential research themes may include:

  • Conflict-related sexual and gender-based violence
  • Violence against women in displacement settings
  • Climate-induced disasters and gender-based violence
  • Humanitarian protection and displacement
  • Migration and trafficking
  • Prevention and response strategies for violence against women
  • Indigenous and survivor-centred methodologies

Scholarship Benefits

Recipients may receive:

Annual Stipend

  • Approximately AUD $39,069 per year
  • Paid in fortnightly instalments

International Student Fee Coverage

International recipients may be recommended for a Higher Degree Research (HDR) Fee Remission Merit Scholarship covering international tuition fees for the standard duration of the PhD program.

Relocation Support

Eligible recipients may receive:

  • Up to AUD $1,000 for domestic students
  • Up to AUD $2,500 for international students

to assist with relocation expenses when moving to commence their studies.

Additional Opportunities

Scholars will benefit from:

  • Membership in the CEVAW research community
  • Collaboration with leading academics and practitioners
  • Access to specialized research ethics and training programs
  • Cross-disciplinary mentoring opportunities
  • Networking with global partners and researchers
  • Opportunities for publications and conference participation
  • Engagement with policymakers, NGOs, and community organizations

Eligibility Criteria

Applicants must:

  • Be a domestic or international student.
  • Demonstrate expertise or strong interest in the elimination of violence against women in migration, displacement, or trafficking contexts.
  • Have completed a Master’s degree with a substantial research component, or equivalent qualifications.
  • Meet ANU PhD admission requirements.
  • Possess strong academic and research capabilities.

Priority consideration will be given to applicants who:

  • Have lived experience of displacement.
  • Are Pasifika scholars.
  • Are Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples.
  • Are First Nations peoples.
  • Come from communities within the Indo-Pacific region.

Why Apply?

This scholarship offers a unique opportunity to:

  • Conduct impactful research addressing major global challenges.
  • Join one of Australia’s leading Centres of Excellence.
  • Work alongside internationally recognized researchers.
  • Influence policy and practice related to violence prevention and protection.
  • Build expertise in migration, displacement, and gender studies.
  • Contribute to meaningful social change across the Indo-Pacific.

Application Period

Applications are open from:

June 22, 2026 – August 31, 2026

How to Apply

Interested candidates should submit an application for admission to the PhD program at the Australian National University and meet all scholarship requirements before the application deadline. Apply Here 

Contact Information

Professor Bina D’Costa
Centre of Excellence for the Elimination of Violence Against Women (CEVAW)
Australian National University

Email: Bina.dcosta@anu.edu.au

Final Thoughts

The PhD Scholarship on Violence Against Women and Displacement at ANU presents an exceptional opportunity for aspiring researchers dedicated to advancing gender justice, humanitarian protection, and evidence-based policy solutions. Through generous funding, expert supervision, and access to the CEVAW network, successful candidates will contribute to groundbreaking research that helps prevent violence against women and supports vulnerable populations across Australia and the Indo-Pacific region.

Application Deadline: August 31, 2026. Apply early and prepare a strong research proposal aligned with CEVAW’s mission of eliminating violence against women.

Discover more scholarship opportunities on the OFY Webpage .

item.content:encoded:
CoCreate Pitch 2026: Apply for the World’s Largest Product-Based Startup Competition and Compete for Over $1 Million in Prizes

Entrepreneurs, startup founders, small business owners, and innovative students from around the world now have an incredible opportunity to showcase their ideas on a global stage through the CoCreate Pitch 2026 competition. Recognized as the world’s largest product-based startup competition, CoCreate Pitch 2026 offers participants the chance to compete for a prize pool worth more than $1,000,000 while gaining international exposure, networking opportunities, mentorship, and access to industry-leading investors and business leaders.

The competition is designed to empower innovators by helping them transform ideas into successful businesses using AI-powered tools provided through Accio Work. Whether you already have an established product, an early-stage startup idea, or you’re a student with an innovative concept, CoCreate Pitch 2026 provides a platform to accelerate your entrepreneurial journey.

Participants will pitch their products before renowned investors, entrepreneurs, CEOs, business executives, and global innovators for a chance to secure significant funding and valuable business support.

About CoCreate Pitch 2026

CoCreate Pitch is a global startup competition focused specifically on product-based businesses. The competition combines artificial intelligence, entrepreneurship, innovation, and investment to help founders build and scale businesses capable of making an impact worldwide.

Through the AI-powered Accio Work platform, applicants can simplify the application process, refine their business ideas, and prepare competitive submissions within minutes.

Since its launch, CoCreate Pitch has grown into one of the largest startup competitions globally, attracting:

  • More than 60,000 small and medium-sized businesses worldwide
  • Over 6,500 media reports covering the competition
  • Thousands of innovative founders across multiple continents

Total Prize Pool

CoCreate Pitch 2026 offers a total prize pool exceeding:

Over $1,000,000

Each regional competition awards:

  • Gold Prize: $200,000
  • Silver Prize: $100,000
  • Bronze Prize: $50,000

Additionally:

  • Every other finalist receives $10,000.

Prize Distribution:

All prizes are awarded as:

  • 50% Cash
  • 50% Alibaba.com credits/coupons

This combination allows winners to receive direct financial support while also accessing business resources for sourcing, manufacturing, and scaling operations.

Competition Tracks

Applicants can compete under one of three categories.

1. General SMEs Track

Designed for:

  • Small businesses
  • Medium-sized enterprises
  • Businesses ready to expand into larger markets

Ideal for companies with existing products looking to scale internationally.

2. 0-to-1 Startup Track

Perfect for:

  • Early-stage founders
  • Individuals with innovative product ideas
  • Entrepreneurs building products from scratch

Participants can leverage Accio Work’s AI capabilities to transform raw ideas into viable business concepts.

3. Student Track

Created specifically for:

  • University students
  • College students
  • Current students developing innovative products

This category encourages the next generation of entrepreneurs to commercialize creative ideas.

Why You Should Apply

Participants gain much more than financial rewards.

Benefits include:

  • Opportunity to compete for over $1 million in prizes
  • International recognition
  • Exposure to global investors
  • Access to experienced judges
  • Business networking opportunities
  • Product validation
  • AI-assisted application support
  • International media exposure
  • Potential investment opportunities
  • Access to Alibaba.com business resources
  • Opportunity to pitch before influential business leaders

APPLY HERE

For more information about this opportunity visit CoCreate Pitch website HERE

For more global competition like this, visit OFY Website HERE

Previous Judges

One of the biggest attractions of CoCreate Pitch is its world-class judging panel.

Past judges have included:

  • Simu Liu – Actor, Writer, Investor
  • Rio Ferdinand – Former International Footballer and Strategic Investor
  • Daymond John – Founder & CEO of FUBU and Shark Tank Investor
  • Lori Greiner – Shark Tank Investor, Inventor, Entrepreneur and Humanitarian
  • Sara Davies – Founder of Crafter’s Companion
  • Everette Taylor – CEO of Kickstarter
  • Alistair Brownlee – Founder of truefuels and Two-Time Olympic Triathlon Champion
  • Stephanie Mehta – CEO and Chief Content Officer of Inc. and Fast Company
  • Eric Larchevêque – Co-founder of Ledger and Serial Entrepreneur

Their expertise provides participants with valuable feedback and exposure to influential business decision-makers.

Global Competition Locations

CoCreate Pitch 2026 will be held across multiple international locations:

  • Los Angeles
  • London
  • Seoul
  • Jakarta
  • Kuala Lumpur

Additional locations may be announced in the future.

Competition Timeline

Los Angeles

  • Applications Open: May 7, 2026
  • Application Deadline: July 25, 2026
  • Finalists Announced: August 10, 2026
  • Event Dates: September 9–10, 2026

London

  • Applications Open: May 7, 2026
  • Application Deadline: October 5, 2026
  • Finalists Announced: October 20, 2026
  • Event Dates: November 19–20, 2026

Seoul

  • Applications Open: May 28, 2026
  • Application Deadline: July 25, 2026
  • Finalists Announced: August 10, 2026
  • Event Date: August 25, 2026

Jakarta

  • Applications Open: June 18, 2026
  • Application Deadline: August 25, 2026
  • Finalists Announced: September 10, 2026
  • Event Date: September 30, 2026

Kuala Lumpur

  • Applications Open: June 18, 2026
  • Application Deadline: August 25, 2026
  • Finalists Announced: September 10, 2026
  • Event Date: October 15, 2026

How to Apply

The application process consists of four simple steps.

Step 1: Download Accio Work

Applicants must download and register on Accio Work.

New users receive:

  • 1,000 bonus credits free upon registration.

Step 2: Complete the Application

Use the AI assistant within Accio Work to complete the application.

The AI-powered process takes approximately five minutes.

Step 3: Selection Process

Regional finalists will be selected as follows:

United States and Europe

  • Top 20 finalists

Korea, Indonesia and Malaysia

  • Top 10 finalists

Step 4: Final Pitch

Selected finalists will present a:

  • 90-second product pitch

before a panel of internationally recognized judges.

Past Success Stories

Harrison Nott – Cool Towel

Winner of the 2025 Europe Grand Prize.

Inspired by heatwaves, Harrison built a modern cooling towel business generating approximately £200,000 in annual revenue by the age of 15.

Christian Reed – Reekon Tools

Winner of the 2025 United States Grand Prize.

Christian transformed a zero-cost garage side project into a crowdfunding campaign exceeding $1.2 million before building a successful hardware company.

Benedikt Freiherr Taets von Amerongen – Trainom GmbH

Europe Athlete Track Winner.

Through CoCreate Pitch, Benedikt expanded awareness of CALIRING, an innovative two-in-one fitness device that combines suspension and free-position training while connecting with new partners.

Why CoCreate Pitch Stands Out

Unlike traditional startup competitions, CoCreate Pitch combines:

  • Artificial Intelligence
  • Global networking
  • Product innovation
  • Investor exposure
  • International media visibility
  • Business acceleration
  • Entrepreneur education
  • Practical funding opportunities

It focuses specifically on product-based businesses, making it ideal for founders seeking both investment and market expansion.

Frequently Asked Questions

Applicants commonly ask:

  • Do I need separate CoCreate tickets after registering?
  • Can I apply for multiple regional events?
  • How do I submit my application?
  • How do I claim the 1,000 bonus credits?
  • Can I edit my submitted application?

Applicants may contact regional support teams for additional assistance depending on their competition location.

Conclusion

CoCreate Pitch 2026 represents one of the most significant opportunities available to entrepreneurs, startup founders, students, and small businesses looking to showcase innovative products on a global platform. With over $1 million in prizes, AI-powered application support, international exposure, networking with world-renowned investors, and opportunities to pitch before globally recognized judges, the competition provides much more than financial rewards. It offers a pathway for innovators to transform ideas into scalable businesses while gaining valuable connections and credibility in the global startup ecosystem. Entrepreneurs with product-based ideas should take advantage of this opportunity and submit their applications before the relevant regional deadline.

item.content:encoded:
The Commonwealth Scholarship Commission (CSC) in the UK has opened applications for the Commonwealth Startup Fellowships 2026, a prestigious six-month entrepreneurship programme designed to support and accelerate high-potential startups from low and middle income Commonwealth countries. Delivered in partnership with Imperial College London, the Fellowship combines immersive in-person experiences with online learning to help founders strengthen their businesses, build global networks, improve investment readiness, and create jobs in their home countries.

The programme is specifically designed for ambitious entrepreneurs who are ready to take their startups to the next level. Through expert-led training, business development support, practical learning opportunities, and international networking, participants will gain the knowledge and skills needed to scale sustainable ventures that contribute to economic growth and innovation across the Commonwealth.

One representative from each selected startup will participate in a two-week bootcamp in Accra, Ghana, followed by a week-long capstone event at the conclusion of the programme. Throughout the six months, Fellows will benefit from mentorship, learning sessions, and engagement with a global entrepreneurial community.

If you are building an innovative startup with the potential to create employment and generate social or economic impact, this Fellowship provides an outstanding opportunity to gain world-class entrepreneurial support.

About the Commonwealth Startup Fellowships

The Commonwealth Startup Fellowships are an initiative of the Commonwealth Scholarship Commission (CSC) in the UK), delivered in collaboration with Imperial College London.

The programme seeks to strengthen entrepreneurship ecosystems across Commonwealth countries by equipping startup founders with the knowledge, skills, networks, and confidence needed to grow successful businesses.

Unlike traditional business training programmes, the Fellowship combines intensive in-person experiences with flexible online learning, allowing entrepreneurs to continue managing their businesses while participating in structured leadership and business development activities.

By the end of the Fellowship, participants are expected to have significantly enhanced their entrepreneurial capabilities, improved their business models, strengthened their investment readiness, and expanded their international networks.

Fellowship Overview

Fellowship Detail Information
Programme Commonwealth Startup Fellowships 2026
Organizers Commonwealth Scholarship Commission (CSC) in the UK & Imperial College London
Duration Six months
Format Hybrid (Online learning plus in-person activities)
Bootcamp Location Accra, Ghana
Capstone Events One-week in-person programme
Target Participants Startup founders from eligible Commonwealth countries
Goal Support startup growth, business scaling, investment readiness, and job creation

Purpose of the Commonwealth Startup Fellowships

The Fellowship is designed to help founders of high-potential startups strengthen their entrepreneurial capacity while developing businesses that contribute to economic development in their home countries.

The programme aims to help entrepreneurs:

  • Scale innovative businesses successfully.
  • Improve entrepreneurial and leadership skills.
  • Build sustainable business models.
  • Strengthen investment readiness.
  • Learn effective pitching techniques.
  • Access international business networks.
  • Create employment opportunities.
  • Contribute to innovation and economic growth within Commonwealth countries.

What the Fellowship Offers

Participants will benefit from a comprehensive entrepreneurship development experience combining practical learning, networking, mentorship, and business growth support.

Key features include:

Six-Month Entrepreneurship Programme

Selected Fellows will participate in a structured six-month programme designed to help startup founders strengthen both their businesses and leadership skills.

The programme combines:

  • Online learning.
  • Practical business development.
  • Networking opportunities.
  • In-person training.
  • Collaborative learning experiences.

Hybrid Learning Experience

The Fellowship blends digital learning with immersive face-to-face activities.

Participants will experience:

  • Interactive online sessions.
  • Expert-led workshops.
  • Collaborative learning.
  • Business development exercises.
  • Networking opportunities.

This hybrid model allows entrepreneurs to continue managing their ventures while benefiting from international training.

Two-Week Bootcamp in Ghana

One representative from every selected startup must attend a mandatory two-week bootcamp in:

Accra, Ghana

The bootcamp provides intensive entrepreneurial learning, collaboration, and networking opportunities designed to strengthen participants’ businesses.

Capstone Programme

Towards the end of the Fellowship, participants will attend a week-long capstone event.

The capstone provides opportunities to:

  • Present business progress.
  • Demonstrate entrepreneurial growth.
  • Engage with mentors.
  • Connect with investors and fellow entrepreneurs.
  • Celebrate programme achievements.

Learning Outcomes

By the conclusion of the Fellowship, entrepreneurs are expected to be able to:

  • Scale their startups more effectively.
  • Deliver compelling business pitches.
  • Apply modern entrepreneurial strategies.
  • Strengthen business leadership.
  • Build international business partnerships.
  • Expand professional networks.
  • Increase the potential for job creation within their home countries.

Programme Partners

Commonwealth Scholarship Commission (CSC)

The Commonwealth Scholarship Commission supports educational and professional development opportunities across the Commonwealth while promoting sustainable development and international collaboration.

Imperial College London

Imperial College London brings internationally recognized expertise in innovation, entrepreneurship, business acceleration, and startup development to the programme.

Together, the two organizations provide participants with a high-quality entrepreneurial learning experience.

International Networking Opportunities

One of the major strengths of the Fellowship is its emphasis on international networking.

Participants will have opportunities to connect with:

  • Entrepreneurs from across the Commonwealth.
  • Startup founders.
  • Business experts.
  • Innovation specialists.
  • Entrepreneurship mentors.
  • Investors.
  • Business support organizations.
  • Academic experts.

These relationships can continue well beyond the Fellowship itself and contribute to long-term business growth.

Who Should Apply?

The Commonwealth Startup Fellowships are designed for entrepreneurs leading promising startups in eligible Commonwealth countries.

The programme is particularly suitable for founders who:

  • Lead high-potential startups.
  • Want to scale their businesses.
  • Are committed to innovation.
  • Seek international business exposure.
  • Wish to improve their investment readiness.
  • Want to create employment opportunities.
  • Are interested in joining a global entrepreneurial network.

Attendance Requirements

Applicants should note that participation requires commitment throughout the programme.

Successful startups must ensure that:

  • One representative from the business participates in the mandatory two-week bootcamp in Accra, Ghana.
  • The same representative attends the week-long capstone events at the end of the programme.
  • Participants actively engage in the online learning components during the six-month programme.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should complete the official application through the Commonwealth Scholarship Commission.

Before submitting an application, prospective candidates are encouraged to:

  1. Review all programme information.

item.content:encoded:
The African Water Facility (AWF) has officially launched its 2026 Call for Proposals (CfP) under the AWF 2026–2030 Strategy, providing an exciting funding opportunity for eligible institutions across Africa to develop high-impact, investment-ready water and sanitation projects.The initiative seeks to strengthen Africa’s water and sanitation investment pipeline by supporting innovative projects capable of attracting downstream financing while improving access to safe water, enhancing sanitation services, strengthening climate resilience, and promoting sustainable and inclusive development. Administered by the African Development Bank (AfDB) on behalf of the African Ministers’ Council on Water (AMCOW), the African Water Facility continues to play a critical role in transforming project concepts into bankable investments that deliver lasting benefits to communities across the continent.

Organizations involved in water security, sanitation, public infrastructure, and institutional development are encouraged to submit concept notes before the application deadline.

About the African Water Facility (AWF)

The African Water Facility is a specialized initiative established by the African Ministers’ Council on Water (AMCOW) and administered by the African Development Bank Group.

Its mission is to mobilize investments that improve water security and sanitation services throughout Africa by supporting the preparation of quality projects that are attractive to investors and development partners.

Rather than financing large-scale infrastructure directly, the Facility focuses on helping organizations prepare strong, investment-ready projects capable of attracting significant future financing from governments, development finance institutions, and private investors.

Through the 2026–2030 Strategy, AWF aims to accelerate progress toward sustainable water management while contributing to climate resilience and improved livelihoods across the continent.

Purpose of the 2026 Call for Proposals

The 2026 Call for Proposals is designed to build a stronger pipeline of bankable water and sanitation projects throughout Africa.

The initiative seeks projects that can:

  • Accelerate access to investment financing.
  • Improve water and sanitation services.
  • Strengthen climate resilience.
  • Promote sustainable infrastructure development.
  • Support inclusive economic growth.
  • Enhance institutional capacity.
  • Generate long-term development impact.
  • Attract downstream public and private investment.

Successful projects will contribute to transforming innovative project concepts into investment-ready operations capable of securing additional financing.

Funding Available

The African Water Facility will provide grant financing to selected projects.

AWF Contribution

Each successful project may receive:

  • Grant funding of up to EUR 1 million.

The funding is intended to support project preparation activities that increase investment readiness and improve the likelihood of securing larger financing for implementation.

Priority Areas

The 2026 Call for Proposals focuses on six strategic priority areas.

1. Project Preparation and Investment Readiness

Projects that strengthen technical, financial, environmental, and institutional preparation to make investments bankable.

2. Climate-Resilient Water and Sanitation Systems

Projects that improve the resilience of water supply and sanitation infrastructure against climate-related risks such as droughts, floods, and changing weather patterns.

3. Innovative Financing and Catalytic Investments

Initiatives that introduce innovative financial approaches capable of mobilizing additional investment from development partners and the private sector.

4. Governance and Institutional Strengthening

Projects that improve governance systems, institutional effectiveness, planning, management, and regulatory capacity within the water and sanitation sector.

5. Inclusive and Sustainable Service Delivery

Projects designed to expand equitable access to quality water and sanitation services while ensuring long-term sustainability.

6. Sanitation Sector Transformation

Innovative initiatives that improve sanitation infrastructure, services, planning, and investment to address sanitation challenges across Africa.

Who Should Apply?

The Call for Proposals welcomes applications from eligible institutions operating within Africa, including:

  • Regional Member Countries (RMCs)
  • Public institutions
  • Water utilities
  • River basin organizations
  • Other eligible entities involved in water and sanitation development

Organizations with strong project concepts that can be developed into investment-ready operations are encouraged to apply.

Geographic Scope

The funding opportunity is exclusively focused on projects implemented within Africa.

Applicants should demonstrate how their proposed project contributes to improving water security and sanitation outcomes on the continent.

Why Apply?

Participating organizations can benefit from several advantages, including:

  • Access to grant financing of up to EUR 1 million.
  • Support in preparing investment-ready projects.
  • Increased opportunities to mobilize larger downstream financing.
  • Strengthened institutional and technical capacity.
  • Improved project bankability.
  • Enhanced climate resilience.
  • Better water and sanitation service delivery.
  • Contribution to sustainable and inclusive development across Africa.

Required Application Documents

Applicants should prepare the following documents:

  • Completed Concept Note.
  • Official AWF Concept Note Template.
  • Supporting documentation required under the Call for Proposals.

Applicants are encouraged to carefully review the complete Call for Proposals before preparing their submissions.

How to Apply

To submit a proposal, applicants should follow these steps:

Step 1

Review the full 2026 Call for Proposals to understand the eligibility requirements, funding priorities, and evaluation criteria.

Step 2

Download the official Concept Note Template.

Step 3

Prepare a high-quality concept note that clearly demonstrates:

  • Project objectives.
  • Expected development impact.
  • Investment readiness.
  • Alignment with AWF priority areas.
  • Potential to mobilize downstream financing.

Step 4

Submit the completed Concept Note before the application deadline to:

African Water Facility (AWF), African Development Bank Group

Email:
africanwaterfacility@afdb.org

CC:

  • Mr. Samuel Blazyk, Officer in Charge, AWF
  • Ms. Hellen Njiwa, Principal Monitoring, Evaluation and Project Portfolio Management Officer
  • Ms. Diane Arjoon, Principal Rural Water Security Officer

Important Funding Information

Funding Type

Grant Financing

Maximum Grant Amount

Up to EUR 1 million per project.

Geographic Coverage

Africa

Eligible Applicants

Regional Member Countries, public institutions, utilities, basin organizations, and other eligible entities.

Learn more about the opportunity HERE

Application Deadline

Deadline: 10 September 2026

Applicants are encouraged to begin preparing their concept notes early to allow sufficient time for developing strong, investment-ready proposals before submission.

Conclusion

The African Water Facility 2026 Call for Proposals presents an outstanding opportunity for African governments, public institutions, utilities, and water sector organizations to secure grant funding that transforms promising project ideas into bankable investments. By supporting project preparation, climate resilience, governance reforms, innovative financing, and sustainable service delivery, the Facility is helping build a stronger pipeline of water and sanitation investments across Africa. Eligible organizations with innovative, high-impact project concepts should take advantage of this opportunity to access up to EUR 1 million in grant financing and contribute to improving water security, sanitation services, and sustainable development across the continent. Interested applicants should review the Call for Proposals, prepare a compelling Concept Note, and submit their application before 10 September 2026.

For more GRANTS OPPORTUNITY click HERE

item.content:encoded:
Individuals who are passionate about creating meaningful change in the issues they care about will soon have an opportunity to join one of the world’s most respected leadership and research fellowships. The Churchill Fellowship offers motivated individuals the chance to explore innovative ideas, learn from leading experts across the globe, and return home with practical knowledge that can transform communities, organizations, and public policy.

The Churchill Fellowship is widely recognized as a unique opportunity that empowers people from diverse backgrounds to investigate solutions to pressing social, economic, environmental, educational, cultural, and health-related challenges. Rather than focusing solely on academic qualifications, the Fellowship emphasizes passion, leadership potential, and a commitment to creating lasting impact.

Applications for the next Churchill Fellowship programme will officially open on 1 September 2026 and close on 20 October 2026. Individuals interested in becoming Fellows are encouraged to prepare early and sign up for application alerts.

What is the Churchill Fellowship?

A Churchill Fellowship is a prestigious opportunity that enables individuals to explore new ideas by connecting with leading professionals and organizations around the world. Fellows investigate innovative approaches to challenges affecting their communities and bring back practical knowledge that can be adapted and implemented for positive change.

Unlike many traditional academic fellowships, the Churchill Fellowship focuses on real-world impact. Fellows are expected to identify an issue they care deeply about, explore international best practices, and apply what they learn to improve their communities, sectors, or professions.

The Fellowship is designed for individuals who want to:

  • Drive meaningful social change.
  • Learn from global experts.
  • Develop innovative solutions.
  • Strengthen leadership capacity.
  • Create long-term community impact.
  • Expand professional networks.
  • Inspire policy and practice improvements.

It is considered a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity for individuals determined to make a difference.

Why Become a Churchill Fellow?

The Fellowship exists to support individuals who have a genuine desire to solve problems rather than simply study them. Fellows investigate how similar challenges are addressed in other countries and return with ideas that can be adapted within their own communities.

Participants become part of a respected network of Fellows working across numerous disciplines and sectors.

The Fellowship provides opportunities to:

  • Learn directly from world-leading professionals.
  • Build international partnerships.
  • Explore innovative practices.
  • Strengthen leadership skills.
  • Develop evidence-based solutions.
  • Share knowledge with communities.
  • Influence policy discussions.
  • Improve services and systems.
  • Create sustainable social impact.
  • Join a lifelong network of Churchill Fellows.

Areas of Research and Interest

Churchill Fellows undertake research across a broad range of topics. Current areas highlighted by the Fellowship include:

  • Arts and Communities
  • Arts and Culture
  • Children and Young People
  • Children in Care
  • Climate Change
  • Community and Citizenship
  • COVID-19
  • Creative Ageing
  • Disability
  • Early Years Intervention
  • Economy and Enterprise
  • Education and Skills
  • Emergency Response
  • Enterprise and Social Impact
  • Environment and Resources
  • Equity, Diversity and Inclusion

In total, Fellows contribute research across dozens of thematic areas, demonstrating the Fellowship’s commitment to addressing complex global challenges through innovative thinking and practical solutions.

A Fellowship Focused on Impact

The Churchill Fellowship is not simply about international travel or professional development. It is about equipping people to return with practical ideas that improve lives.

Successful Fellows often contribute by:

  • Improving public services.
  • Strengthening community programmes.
  • Developing new educational approaches.
  • Supporting vulnerable populations.
  • Advancing environmental sustainability.
  • Promoting inclusion and diversity.
  • Encouraging innovation in business and enterprise.
  • Supporting cultural development.
  • Influencing national and local policy.
  • Building stronger communities.

The Fellowship encourages participants to translate international learning into measurable local impact.

How the Fellowship Works

Applicants begin by identifying an issue they are passionate about improving.

Once selected, Fellows explore how similar issues are being addressed internationally by engaging with experts, organizations, institutions, practitioners, and innovators.

Following their research, Fellows return to share their findings, implement new ideas, and contribute to positive change within their sectors and communities.

This practical approach ensures that knowledge gained through the Fellowship benefits society well beyond the individual participant.

Application Timeline

Interested applicants should take note of the official application period:

  • Applications Open: 1st September 2026
  • Application Deadline: 20th October 2026

Prospective applicants are encouraged to prepare their ideas early and register for application alerts to receive updates regarding the application process.

Preparing a Strong Application

Although detailed application guidance is provided separately by the Churchill Fellowship, prospective applicants should begin preparing by:

  1. Identifying an important issue they want to address.
  2. Demonstrating a genuine commitment to creating change.
  3. Researching existing challenges within their community or professional sector.
  4. Developing a clear vision of the knowledge they wish to gain internationally.
  5. Explaining how the Fellowship will create lasting impact after completion.
  6. Preparing examples of leadership, initiative, or community engagement.
  7. Reviewing the Fellowship’s current programme areas to ensure alignment.

APPLY HERE

Why This Fellowship Matters

Many social challenges require fresh thinking and practical solutions. The Churchill Fellowship recognizes that some of the best ideas can emerge through international collaboration and shared learning.

By supporting passionate individuals to learn from global leaders, the Fellowship strengthens communities, encourages innovation, and creates lasting improvements across numerous sectors.

Whether addressing education, climate change, healthcare, social inclusion, entrepreneurship, or community development, Churchill Fellows become part of a growing movement dedicated to positive change.

Visit HERE for more information about the Become a Churchill Fellow 2026–2027 Fellowship.

Stay Updated

Individuals interested in applying are encouraged to sign up for the Fellowship’s application alerts to receive notifications about application opening dates, programme updates, and additional guidance before the next application cycle begins.

Deadline

20th October 2026.

Conclusion

The Churchill Fellowship represents an exceptional opportunity for individuals who are committed to solving real-world problems through international learning and collaboration. Rather than offering a traditional academic experience, the Fellowship empowers changemakers to explore innovative solutions from around the world and translate them into meaningful action within their own communities. If you have a strong vision for creating positive impact and are eager to learn from global experts, the Churchill Fellowship could be the ideal platform to turn your ideas into lasting change. With applications opening on 1st September 2026 and closing on 20th October 2026, prospective applicants should begin preparing early to maximize their chances of success.

For more global Fellowship opportunities, visit OFY HERE.

item.content:encoded:
Artificial Intelligence is fundamentally transforming industries, redefining job roles, and reshaping how professionals collaborate, communicate, and solve complex challenges. As organizations increasingly integrate AI into everyday operations, professionals are expected to possess not only technical knowledge but also the leadership, communication, ethical decision-making, and critical thinking skills necessary to thrive in this rapidly changing environment.

Recognizing this growing demand, Aspire Institute has launched the Leadership Accelerator Powered by AI (LAPA) 2026, an innovative leadership development program designed specifically for early-career professionals who want to become future-ready leaders.

Unlike traditional AI courses that focus exclusively on technology or leadership programs that emphasize soft skills alone, the Leadership Accelerator integrates both disciplines into one practical learning experience. Participants learn how to use AI responsibly while simultaneously developing the leadership competencies needed to succeed in today’s evolving workplace.

Whether you are a recent graduate, an emerging professional, or an organization investing in future leaders, this accelerator provides an opportunity to gain industry-relevant skills from globally recognized experts while building practical solutions to real workplace challenges.

What is the Aspire Leadership Accelerator Powered by AI?

The Leadership Accelerator Powered by AI is an intensive 30-hour virtual leadership development program delivered over eight weeks through a combination of self-paced learning, live cohort discussions, peer collaboration, and applied project work.

The curriculum has been carefully designed to prepare professionals for workplaces increasingly driven by artificial intelligence by combining AI literacy with leadership development.

Throughout the program, participants engage in:

  • Self-paced online learning
  • Live cohort discussions
  • Peer-to-peer learning
  • Practical AI applications
  • Real-world leadership scenarios
  • Industry masterclasses
  • Hands-on capstone project

Instead of merely learning about AI, participants actively apply AI tools to solve authentic workplace problems while strengthening leadership capabilities such as communication, resilience, negotiation, ethical leadership, teamwork, and strategic decision-making.

Program Overview

The Leadership Accelerator offers an accessible and flexible learning experience suitable for busy professionals.

Duration

  • 8 weeks
  • 30 learning hours
  • Approximately 4 hours per week

Learning Format

The program combines:

  • Virtual learning
  • Self-paced coursework
  • Cohort-based learning
  • Live masterclasses
  • Interactive discussions
  • Practical projects

Participants study using the AI-native Sana Learning Management System, which includes:

  • AI-powered coaching
  • 24/7 AI tutor
  • Intelligent learning support
  • Interactive learning experiences
  • AI role-play simulations for communication and negotiation practice

Comprehensive Curriculum

The Leadership Accelerator consists of seven progressive modules followed by a practical capstone project.

Week 1: Foundations of Artificial Intelligence

Participants begin by understanding:

  • Types of Artificial Intelligence
  • Prompt engineering
  • Responsible AI
  • AI bias evaluation
  • Decision-support systems
  • Practical AI applications in professional environments

This foundational module equips learners with the knowledge needed to confidently integrate AI into their daily work while understanding its limitations and ethical implications.

Weeks 2–3: Communication, Productivity, and Team Dynamics

Participants strengthen essential workplace skills including:

  • Professional communication
  • Effective listening
  • Team collaboration
  • Time management
  • Delegation
  • Priority management
  • Productivity systems
  • AI-enhanced workflows

The module demonstrates how AI can support better communication and improve workplace efficiency without replacing human judgment.

Weeks 4 and 7: Peer Learning and Leadership Reflection

Leadership development extends beyond classroom instruction.

Participants engage in:

  • Collaborative discussions
  • Reflection exercises
  • Community learning
  • Leadership feedback
  • Interpersonal skill development
  • Self-awareness activities

These experiences encourage participants to learn from diverse perspectives while strengthening emotional intelligence and collaborative leadership.

Weeks 5–6: Resilience, Negotiation, and Ethical Leadership

Professionals learn how to:

  • Lead under uncertainty
  • Make ethical decisions
  • Build resilience
  • Conduct negotiations
  • Navigate ambiguity
  • Apply AI to strategic thinking
  • Solve complex workplace challenges

Negotiation exercises are reinforced using AI-powered simulations before participants apply these techniques in real professional situations.

Week 8: Capstone Project and Live Masterclasses

The program concludes with an applied leadership project.

Participants:

  • Identify a real challenge within their organization, workplace, or community.
  • Design an AI-enabled solution.
  • Develop an implementation strategy.
  • Present their project.
  • Receive insights from industry experts through live masterclasses.

This capstone ensures participants graduate with practical experience rather than theoretical knowledge alone.

Learn from Global Industry Leaders

The accelerator is taught by accomplished executives, entrepreneurs, investors, and leadership experts from globally recognized organizations.

Faculty members include professionals such as:

  • Angel investors
  • Harvard Business School Executive Fellows
  • Digital transformation leaders
  • Former Microsoft executives
  • CEOs
  • Technology innovators
  • Board directors
  • Leadership coaches

These instructors contribute real-world expertise that bridges theory and workplace practice.

What Makes This Program Different?

Unlike many professional development programs, Aspire’s Leadership Accelerator combines AI education with leadership development in a single integrated experience.

Participants develop:

  • Practical AI readiness
  • Leadership confidence
  • Ethical judgment
  • Strategic thinking
  • Communication excellence
  • High-performing teamwork
  • Workplace productivity
  • Negotiation capability
  • Critical thinking
  • Decision-making skills

The program emphasizes practical application rather than passive learning, allowing participants to solve authentic workplace challenges throughout the course.

Benefits of Joining the Program

Participants graduate with numerous professional advantages, including:

  • Practical AI application skills
  • Prompt engineering expertise
  • Responsible AI evaluation skills
  • Strong workplace communication abilities
  • Leadership frameworks
  • Productivity systems
  • Negotiation strategies
  • AI-supported problem-solving techniques
  • Team leadership experience
  • Capstone project portfolio
  • Certificate signed by Aspire co-founders and Harvard Business School faculty

Why Organizations Are Investing in This Program

Organizations can enroll emerging professionals to build future-ready talent.

Benefits include:

  • Developing AI-fluent employees
  • Improving communication and leadership capacity
  • Enhancing collaboration
  • Supporting employee retention
  • Strengthening long-term talent pipelines
  • Preparing professionals for AI-integrated workplaces

Participants immediately apply newly acquired skills to real organizational challenges through the capstone project.

Visit HERE for more information about the Aspire Leadership Accelerator Powered by AI 2026.

Who Should Apply?

The Leadership Accelerator is ideal for:

  • Early-career professionals
  • Young leaders
  • Recent graduates
  • Aspire Leaders Program graduates
  • Organizations investing in employee development
  • Universities
  • Academies
  • Employers building leadership pipelines

The program accommodates both individual applicants and organizational cohorts.

APPLY HERE

Program Cost

The investment for individual participants is:

US$100 per participant

Additional opportunities include:

  • Discounts for Aspire Leaders Program graduates
  • Volume discounts for organizations enrolling multiple participants
  • Private cohort options for organizations
  • University partnership packages

Technical Requirements

Participants should have:

  • A stable internet connection.
  • A laptop or device with sufficient memory.
  • The ability to access the Sana AI-native learning platform throughout the eight-week program.

Important Dates

The program offers multiple cohorts.

  • Cohort 3 runs from September 14 to November 9, 2026.
  • Payment options for Cohort 3 become available on June 15, 2026.

Application Deadline: The source does not specify a final application deadline. Interested applicants are encouraged to reserve their seat as early as possible.

Conclusion

The Aspire Leadership Accelerator Powered by AI 2026 offers an innovative professional development experience that combines artificial intelligence, leadership, communication, collaboration, ethical decision-making, and practical workplace application into one comprehensive program. Through expert-led instruction, AI-powered learning technologies, peer collaboration, and an applied capstone project, participants gain the knowledge and practical experience needed to thrive in AI-driven workplaces.

Whether you are a recent graduate preparing for your career, an early-career professional seeking leadership advancement, or an organization developing future talent, this globally accessible accelerator provides an affordable and practical pathway to becoming a confident, AI-ready leader. By completing the program, participants not only earn a prestigious certificate but also develop real-world solutions and leadership capabilities that can create lasting impact within their organizations and communities.

item.content:encoded:
The Council of Europe Youth Department is inviting applications for the third edition of the Youth Advocacy for Democracy and Human Rights Training Course, which will take place at the European Youth Centre Strasbourg, France, from 27 September to 4 October 2026.

Organized under the Youth Revitalising Democracy Project, this fully funded international training programme is designed to strengthen the advocacy skills of young activists, youth leaders, and members of youth civil society organizations who are committed to promoting democracy, human rights, and meaningful youth participation in public decision-making.

The training course will be held alongside the Plenary Session of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe, providing participants with a unique opportunity to gain insights into democratic institutions while learning practical advocacy strategies from experts and peers.

If you are passionate about advancing democratic values, protecting human rights, and increasing youth participation in governance, this is an excellent opportunity to build your skills, expand your network, and contribute to positive democratic change.

About the Training Course

The Youth Advocacy for Democracy and Human Rights Training Course forms part of the Council of Europe Youth Department’s broader efforts to strengthen youth engagement in democratic life.

The programme recognizes that young people and youth organizations play an essential role in promoting democracy, defending human rights, and ensuring that youth perspectives are reflected in policy-making at local, national, and international levels.

Through interactive learning, practical exercises, peer exchange, and engagement with Council of Europe institutions, participants will strengthen their ability to design and implement effective advocacy initiatives that promote democratic participation and human rights.

The course also contributes directly to the objectives of the Youth Revitalising Democracy Project, which seeks to remove barriers to youth participation in politics and strengthen structures that enable young people to influence public decision-making.

Aim of the Programme

The primary aim of the training course is to strengthen the competencies of youth civil society representatives and young activists in advocating for:

  • Democracy
  • Human rights
  • Youth participation
  • Implementation of Council of Europe standards
  • Inclusive public policies
  • Youth representation in decision-making processes

Participants will also explore ways to integrate youth perspectives across the work of the Council of Europe while promoting democratic values within their own communities and countries.

Objectives of the Training Course

Throughout the programme, participants will work toward achieving several important learning objectives, including:

1. Understanding the Council of Europe

Participants will gain a comprehensive understanding of:

  • The Council of Europe
  • Its institutions
  • Democratic governance structures
  • Human rights standards
  • Youth participation mechanisms

2. Strengthening Advocacy Skills

The programme will help participants:

  • Develop human rights-based advocacy skills.
  • Design effective advocacy strategies.
  • Plan advocacy campaigns.
  • Build practical advocacy competencies.
  • Influence policy processes.

3. Learning from Good Practices

Participants will exchange experiences and learn from successful examples of:

  • Human rights advocacy
  • Democratic participation
  • Youth engagement
  • Civic activism
  • Collaboration with policymakers
  • Youth participation structures

4. Engaging with the Youth Revitalising Democracy Project

The training will introduce participants to the ongoing work of the Council of Europe Youth Department and provide opportunities to contribute to future initiatives under the Youth Revitalising Democracy Project.

5. Developing Joint Advocacy Initiatives

Participants will collaborate to design common advocacy actions that contribute to:

  • Increasing youth participation in elections.
  • Removing barriers preventing young people from running for public office.
  • Strengthening youth participation in democratic decision-making.
  • Expanding the implementation of Council of Europe democratic standards.

What Participants Will Learn

The programme combines theoretical knowledge with practical skills development.

Participants can expect sessions covering topics such as:

  • Democracy and democratic institutions

Support includes:

  • Accommodation
  • Meals during the programme

This financial support enables selected participants to fully engage in the learning experience without worrying about major participation costs.

Why You Should Apply

Participating in this programme provides an opportunity to:

  • Develop advanced advocacy skills.
  • Strengthen your understanding of democracy and human rights.
  • Learn directly from Council of Europe experts.
  • Connect with youth leaders from different countries.
  • Exchange experiences with fellow activists.
  • Expand your international professional network.

item.content:encoded:
The CAPSHA South-South Collaboration Innovation Pitch Challenge 2026 is an innovation funding opportunity designed to support creative, demand-driven partnerships that strengthen agricultural research, extension, education, and innovation systems across Africa, Asia, and Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC).

The challenge is organized under the CGIAR Capacity Sharing (CapSha) Accelerator, which promotes a new model of collaboration focused on equitable partnerships, shared knowledge creation, mutual learning, and long-term institutional transformation.

Unlike traditional capacity-building approaches where knowledge is viewed as something transferred from one organization to another, the CapSha Accelerator recognizes that sustainable innovation emerges when institutions collaborate as equal partners. Through this challenge, participants are invited to submit innovative ideas that can improve capacity-sharing approaches between CGIAR and National Agricultural Research Extension and Education Systems (NAREES).

Selected winners will receive grants of up to USD 15,000 to implement their proposed initiatives and contribute to stronger, more resilient, and inclusive food, land, and water systems.

Opportunity Category

Category: Grant / Innovation Challenge

The CAPSHA South-South Collaboration Innovation Pitch Challenge provides financial support through competitive grants awarded to selected innovative partnership proposals.

About the CAPSHA Accelerator

National Agricultural Research Extension and Education Systems (NAREES) play a critical role in advancing sustainable agricultural development, food security, climate resilience, and rural livelihoods.

However, today’s global challenges require more than traditional knowledge-sharing methods. Increasing pressures from:

  • Climate change
  • Food insecurity
  • Natural resource challenges
  • Nutrition concerns
  • Changing rural livelihoods
  • The need for sustainable agricultural systems

require new approaches that encourage collaboration, innovation, and shared ownership.

The CGIAR Capacity Sharing (CapSha) Accelerator promotes a partnership-based approach where CGIAR organizations and NAREES institutions work together to:

  • Generate knowledge collaboratively.
  • Exchange expertise and experiences.
  • Adapt innovative solutions to local contexts.
  • Strengthen institutional capacity.
  • Build long-term networks for continuous learning.

The Innovation Pitch Challenge seeks ideas that demonstrate how collaborative capacity-sharing models can transform agricultural research and innovation systems.

Goal of the CAPSHA Innovation Pitch Challenge

The overall goal of the challenge is to identify and support innovative, demand-driven capacity-sharing partnerships that strengthen national research and innovation systems while contributing to CGIAR’s long-term impact agenda.

The initiative aims to encourage partnerships that create practical solutions for strengthening agricultural systems and improving collaboration between institutions across different regions.

Specific Objectives of the Challenge

The CAPSHA South-South Collaboration Innovation Pitch Challenge aims to:

1. Strengthen CGIAR and NAREES Collaboration

The challenge seeks to improve engagement between CGIAR institutions and National Agricultural Research Extension and Education Systems by creating stronger partnerships based on shared priorities.

2. Identify Innovative and Scalable Opportunities

The programme aims to discover ideas that have potential for:

  • Short-term implementation.
  • Medium-term expansion.
  • Long-term investment and sustainability.

3. Promote Equitable Partnerships

The challenge encourages co-creation between CGIAR and NAREES institutions, ensuring that all partners contribute knowledge, expertise, and solutions.

4. Advance South-South and North-South Knowledge Exchange

The programme supports collaboration between institutions across:

  • Africa.
  • Asia.
  • Latin America and the Caribbean.
  • Northern and Southern research institutions.

This promotes mutual learning and strengthens global agricultural innovation networks.

5. Develop Scalable Models for Agricultural Capacity Strengthening

Selected ideas should contribute to stronger:

  • Agricultural research systems.
  • Extension services.
  • Education programmes.
  • Implementation capacities.

6. Build Sustainable Learning Networks

The challenge aims to encourage Communities of Practice and long-term networks that continue knowledge exchange beyond individual projects.

Funding Award

The total available award budget for the challenge is:

USD 45,000

Three grants will be awarded:

  • Africa Region: USD 15,000 grant.
  • Asia Region: USD 15,000 grant.
  • Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC) Region: USD 15,000 grant.

The highest-ranked candidate from each region will receive funding to implement their proposed innovation project.

Eligible Project Ideas

Applicants are encouraged to submit innovative concepts that demonstrate practical approaches to improving capacity sharing and agricultural innovation systems.

Successful proposals should focus on ideas that:

  • Address real challenges within agricultural research and innovation systems.
  • Promote collaboration between institutions.
  • Encourage knowledge exchange and mutual learning.
  • Have potential for scaling and replication.
  • Strengthen food, land, and water systems.
  • Support sustainable development outcomes.

Partnership Approach

The challenge emphasizes collaboration rather than individual institutional efforts.

Projects may involve partnerships between:

  • CGIAR Centers.
  • Universities in the Global North and Global South.
  • Government agencies.
  • Farmer producer organizations.
  • Private sector organizations.
  • Non-governmental organizations (NGOs).
  • Development partners.
  • Regional organizations.

Who Can Apply?

Eligible Applicants

Applications must be led by a National Agricultural Research Extension and Education Systems (NAREES) institution from one of the following regions:

  • Africa.
  • Asia.
  • Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC).

The lead applicant institution may collaborate with additional partners, including research organizations, universities, government institutions, private sector actors, and development organizations.

APPLY HERE

Eligible Regions and Countries

The opportunity is open to eligible institutions located in:

  • African countries.
  • Asian countries.
  • Latin American and Caribbean countries.

The provided information does not specify individual eligible countries; applicants should confirm eligibility according to their regional NAREES institution status.

Eligible Participants

The challenge is suitable for:

  • Agricultural research institutions.
  • National extension systems.
  • Agricultural education institutions.
  • Research and innovation organizations.
  • Universities.
  • Government agencies involved in agriculture.
  • Development organizations working on food systems.
  • Partner organizations collaborating with eligible NAREES institutions.

Important Eligibility Requirement

The application must be led by a NAREES institution. Other organizations may participate as partners but cannot replace the required lead applicant.

Award Benefits

Successful applicants will receive:

  • Funding of up to USD 15,000 for selected regional winners.
  • Support to implement innovative agricultural capacity-sharing initiatives.
  • Opportunities to strengthen international partnerships.
  • Increased visibility within agricultural research and innovation networks.
  • Opportunities to contribute to sustainable food systems transformation.

Application Timeline

Application Period

Applications are open from:

24 July 2026 to 7 August 2026

Deadline: 7 August 2026 at 23:59 Indian Standard Time (IST)

Applicants must submit their proposals before the deadline. Late submissions may not be considered.

Selection Timeline

  • 24 July 2026: Application period opens.
  • 7 August 2026: Application deadline.
  • 13 August 2026: Selected candidates for the pitch side event will be contacted.

Pitch Challenge Selection Process

Submitted proposals will be evaluated based on their alignment with the objectives of the challenge and their ability to demonstrate innovative approaches to capacity sharing.

The challenge focuses on identifying proposals that:

  • Present practical and achievable solutions.
  • Strengthen institutional partnerships.
  • Demonstrate innovation.
  • Support sustainable agricultural development.
  • Create long-term value beyond the project period.

How to Apply

Applicants should prepare and submit innovative proposals according to the challenge requirements.

Interested institutions should ensure that:

  1. The proposal is led by an eligible NAREES institution.
  2. The idea demonstrates strong collaboration potential.
  3. The project addresses capacity-sharing challenges.
  4. The proposal clearly explains expected outcomes and sustainability.

Applicants should follow the official submission process provided by the CAPSHA Accelerator.

Visit HERE to learn more about the CAPSHA South-South Collaboration Innovation Pitch Challenge 2026

Why Participate in the CAPSHA Innovation Pitch Challenge?

The challenge provides an opportunity for agricultural institutions and partners to move beyond traditional capacity-building approaches and develop new models of collaboration.

Through participation, organizations can:

  • Strengthen agricultural innovation systems.
  • Build international partnerships.
  • Develop scalable solutions.
  • Improve knowledge exchange.
  • Support climate-resilient food systems.
  • Contribute to sustainable rural development.

The challenge recognizes that solving complex agricultural challenges requires cooperation between institutions, communities, researchers, and policymakers.

Conclusion

The CAPSHA South-South Collaboration Innovation Pitch Challenge 2026 represents an important opportunity for agricultural research institutions and partners across Africa, Asia, and Latin America and the Caribbean to develop innovative solutions for strengthening capacity sharing and collaboration.

With grants of up to USD 15,000, the challenge supports initiatives that promote equitable partnerships, knowledge exchange, and sustainable transformation of agricultural research and innovation systems.

Eligible NAREES institutions and their partners are encouraged to submit innovative ideas that can contribute to stronger food systems, improved resilience, and long-term global collaboration before the 7 August 2026 deadline.
